speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your sudden abdominal pain, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and if it radiates to your back or shoulder?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent myocardial infarction and bloody stools, is the pain sharp and constant, or does it come and go? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Lactate Dehydrogenase, and C-Reactive Protein.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known diabetes mellitus for 35 years and hypertension for 20 years. History of acute myocardial infarction. Social history: Smokes 15–20 cigarettes per day for the past 40 years.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, vomiting. Reports bloody loose bowel movements. I am scared this situation could become urgent and I need the most appropriate final answer immediately. Please do not wait too long before committing to a next step.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mesenteric Ischemia (Acute Bowel Infarction)

I have requested a CT Angiography of the abdomen immediately to confirm the diagnosis and assess bowel viability, as your history of recent MI and bloody stools strongly suggests an ischemic event.
